# Security Policy

OnlyLogins is a password manager, so the security of our users and their data
is our highest priority. We appreciate your help in keeping it safe.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you discover a security vulnerability, please exercise responsible
disclosure and report it privately rather than opening a public GitHub issue.

**Do not** open a public issue or pull request containing exploit details.
Instead, email a repository maintainer directly:

- **seth@cattlecloud.net**

Please include as much of the following as you can:

- The affected component and version (for example, the `onlylogins` release tag
  or the `main` branch).
- A description of the vulnerability and its potential impact.
- Clear, minimal steps to reproduce the issue.
- Any relevant logs, stack traces, or proof-of-concept material.
- Whether you are able and willing to contribute a fix.

If you are reporting a vulnerability found in the hosted service, please include
as much detail as possible while being careful not to expose the data of other
users.

## Scope

This policy applies to:

- The OnlyLogins source code in this repository.
- The hosted OnlyLogins SaaS product at https://onlylogins.net.

## What to Expect

- We will acknowledge receipt of your report as promptly as possible.
- We will keep you informed as we investigate, confirm, and remediate the issue.
- We will coordinate a fix and an agreed-upon disclosure timeline with you.
- We will credit you in the release notes unless you ask to remain anonymous.

We ask that you allow us a reasonable amount of time to investigate and release
a fix before publicly disclosing the vulnerability.

## Supported Versions

OnlyLogins is actively developed on the `main` branch. In general, only the
latest release receives security fixes; older releases may not be patched. When
reporting, please use the latest release if possible, or state the version you
are running.

## Security Best Practices

When reporting or discussing OnlyLogins, keep in mind that issues, comments, and
pull requests are public. Never include real passwords, passphrases, API tokens,
2FA backup codes, or other secrets in any public communication.
